body:
## Summary
Replace three hand-kept name-perturbation lists, each wired to a different subset of engines, with ONE perturbation set and ONE registry that every public function taking a candidate must either register an invariance runner in or be exempted from with a written reason - derived from the tree, so a new scorer cannot ship unproven.

## Description
The name-neutrality claim (the AI-Act pack's closed G3) is only as wide as the engines someone remembered to perturb. Today that is match(), fairness_matrix() and analyze_cv(), spread across test_fairness.py, test_name_neutrality.py and matching_eval.py with three different pair lists. Twice already a planted -ová penalty stayed green because it lived in an engine no test perturbed (both recorded in the test files' own docstrings). Meanwhile 41 public functions take a MatchCandidate/CandidateProfile - recruiter ranking, the Fair Rank matrix, the keyless screen that gates automated moves, rematch, winnability, weight proposals - and none of them is perturbed. `pipeline/jobfit/eval/neutrality.py` holds the canonical PERTURBATIONS (union of the three sets), an AST discoverer of candidate-typed public functions, SCORERS (name -> runner + declared carrier paths) and EXEMPT (name -> reason). `test_neutrality_registry.py` asserts completeness, runs every scorer x every perturbation for byte-identity outside the declared carriers, and runs the sentinel second-carrier check. The three existing suites import the set instead of re-typing it.

## Flow
1. discover_candidate_scorers() walks pipeline/jobfit with ast, returns module.func for public defs with a candidate-typed parameter.
2. Completeness: discovered == SCORERS + EXEMPT, disjoint, reasons >= 20 chars.
3. For each SCORER: build the baseline input from the fixed profile named 'Alex Smith', then for each perturbation rebuild with only the name (or gendered prose line) changed, run, pop the declared carriers, canonical-JSON, compare bytes.
4. Sentinel pass: run with 'Zzneutralitynamezz', fail on any path outside the carriers that contains it.
5. matching_eval/_probe_gender and the two suites iterate neutrality.PERTURBATIONS.

## Expected impact
The fairness claim becomes a statement about every candidate-typed function on the tree rather than three of them, and the class 'a new or refactored scorer reads the name' closes at the moment the function is written. The measured probe run on today's tree (screen, rematch, rank, winnability over 5 names x 2 profiles) is neutral, so this lands green and widens the gate.

## Evaluation
Claim: every candidate-typed scorer is either proven name-invariant over one market-specific perturbation set or exempted with a stated reason, and a new one cannot slip in.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no registry, no discoverer; the planted recruiter mutation stays green).
After: 8 of 8.
Method: policy-tighten - node-free Python cases in test_neutrality_registry.py under test:python:gate, plus the planted-mutation case and test:eval:ci.
Result: pending build.
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: Three literal sets: test_fairness.py:113 `_GENDER_PAIRS = (` (Jan Novák/Jana Nováková, accent-stripped, Ing., John/Jane Smith); test_name_neutrality.py:55 `NAME_VARIANTS: dict[str, str] = {` (czech_male, czech_female_ova, vietnamese, ukrainian, arabic, roma_associated, roma_associated_female); matching_eval.py:311 `pairs = [` (3 pairs). AST scan (public top-level defs with a MatchCandidate/CandidateProfileV2/CandidateProfile-annotated parameter, excluding tests/eval/bench/_cli/seed_) = 41 functions across automation(7), insights(1), interview(1), jobseeker(1), live_case(2), match_reasoning(2), matching(13), profile(3), recruiter(3), soft_signals(1), transform(3), weight_proposal(3), winnability(1). Probe run 2026-09-23 (PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, keyless): screen_candidate/rematch_candidate/rank_candidates_for_job/assess_winnability over ['Alex Smith','Jiří Novák','Jana Nováková','Nguyễn Thị Thu Hà','Gejza Horváth'] x (_senior_backend,_student_frontend) -> 0 diffs after removing the name; sentinel carriers found: rank rows '[0].label', soft-signal panel '.display_name', screen [] , rematch [] - so the carrier declarations are small and known today.

title: Fair Rank keys identity on candidate id: a namesake can't erase an eligible hire
acceptance: fairness_check([('a', senior 'Jan Novák'), ('b', junior 'Jan Novák')], senior job) -> koFailed == ['b'], rankingIds == ['a'], ranking == ['Jan Novák'] (today: ranking == [] - the eligible senior vanishes because his KO'd namesake shares the label)
a pool where every label is the transform fallback 'Candidate' (transform.py:262) with one KO-failed member -> rankingIds lists every non-KO id, in mean-descending order
pool-level name neutrality: the same two candidates labelled ('Jan Novák','Petr Svoboda') vs ('Jan Novák','Jan Novák') -> identical rankingIds, koFailed, matrix and mean
fairness_matrix(...) returns 'order', a permutation of range(n) sorted by mean desc, and 'ranking' == [labels[i] for i in order] exactly as today (back-compat for every existing reader)

isFairnessAligned({labels:['Jan Novák','Jan Novák'], candidateIds:['a','b'], rankingIds:['a'], ranking:['Jan Novák'], koFailed:['b'], square 2x2 matrix...}) -> true, so assessRobustness returns 'assessed' when weights vary (today the Python output ranking:[] + koFailed:1 != n:2 -> false -> 'unavailable', i.e. the sealed record says robustness could not be assessed because two people share a name)
isFairnessAligned rejects a rankingIds entry not in candidateIds, a duplicate id, or an id also in koFailed; a legacy blob with NO rankingIds is judged by today's label rule unchanged

robustOrder by id: rankingIds ['b','a'] vs headline ids ['a','b'] with both labels 'Jan Novák' -> 'diverges' (today robustOrderVerdict(['Jan Novák','Jan Novák'], ['Jan Novák','Jan Novák']) says 'agrees' - a swapped namesake order is invisible); legacy payload without ids falls back to the label comparison
the Fair Rank audit table and the robust-order pills key React rows on candidate id, never on label (no duplicate key for namesakes)
premise: pipeline/jobfit/recruiter.py:61-68 collects ko_failed_labels (a set of display labels) and filters matrix['ranking'] by label - every candidate sharing a KO'd candidate's name is dropped

pipeline/jobfit/matching.py:1145 labels = [c.label ...] and :1166 'ranking': [labels[i] for i in order] - the robust order is emitted as names, not ids, while candidateIds exist beside it (recruiter.py:53)
pipeline/jobfit/transform.py:262 label=profile.display_name or 'Candidate' - every unnamed profile shares one label

app/features/shared/groupEvalTypes.ts:76 `if (ranking.length + koCount !== n) return false;` and :78 label-set membership - the namesake drop makes a real matrix read as misaligned, and assessRobustness (:90) then reports 'unavailable'
app/features/hiring/decisions/groupEval/groupEvalHelpers.ts:91-97 robustOrderVerdict compares label strings; app/_lib/group-eval-run.ts:982 recommendedOrder: candidates.map((c) => c.label)
app/features/library/jobs/JobsRecruiterCandidatesFairness.tsx:71 `<tr key={r.label}` and GroupEvalFairnessPanel.tsx:157-160 render ranking by label

the rest of group-eval already moved to ids for exactly this reason: group-eval-run.ts:88 ('by id (not by the non-unique display label)'), :958 comparedIds, groupEvalDelta.test.ts:132 'tracks two candidates with the same label separately by entry id' - the fairness seam is the one left behind

body:
## Summary
The cross-scheme fairness ranking identifies candidates by display name. When two candidates share a name (or both fall back to 'Candidate') and one is knocked out, both disappear from the robust order - and the TS guard then declares the whole matrix misaligned, so the sealed group evaluation says robustness 'could not be assessed'. Key the ranking, the KO exclusion and the order verdict on candidate id end to end.

## Description
Name neutrality is this context's central contract: the name may move nothing. At the single-candidate level it holds; at the pool level it does not. recruiter.fairness_check drops KO-failed candidates from the ranking by LABEL (recruiter.py:61-68), fairness_matrix emits the ranking as labels (matching.py:1166), isFairnessAligned counts ranking + koFailed against n (groupEvalTypes.ts:76), and robustOrderVerdict compares label strings (groupEvalHelpers.ts:91). Measured: two candidates both named 'Jan Novák', one KO'd -> ranking [] ; with distinct names -> ['Jan Novák']. The fix: fairness_matrix adds `order` (indices); fairness_check excludes by index and emits `rankingIds`; the payload gains `recommendedIds`; the TS guard, verdict, panel and Fair Rank table read ids when present and fall back to labels for legacy sealed blobs. A pool-level namesake case joins the neutrality suite so the contract is pinned where it broke.

## Flow
1. matching.fairness_matrix: add 'order': list[int]; 'ranking' unchanged.
2. recruiter.fairness_check: ko_failed index set; rankingIds = [candidateIds[i] for i in order if i not in ko]; ranking = labels of the same.
3. group-eval-run: persist recommendedIds beside recommendedOrder.
4. groupEvalTypes.isFairnessAligned: validate rankingIds (subset of candidateIds, unique, disjoint from koFailed, count + koFailed == n); legacy rule when absent.
5. robustOrderVerdict(rankingIds, headlineIds) with a label fallback; panel + Fair Rank table render labels looked up by id, keyed by id.
6. test_fairness: NamesakePoolTest; test_recruiter + two TS tests pin the payload.

## Expected impact
An eligible candidate can no longer be erased from a sealed fairness audit - or turn the audit into 'could not assess' - because someone else in the pool has the same name. Common Czech names and every unnamed/blinded profile ('Candidate') are exactly the populations this hits; the demo never shows it because seeded names are forced unique.

## Evaluation
Claim: the robust order, KO exclusion and order verdict are functions of candidate identity, not of display name.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (probe: namesake pool -> ranking []).
After: 8 of 8.
Method: contract - Python cases in test_fairness.py/test_recruiter.py under test:python:gate, TS cases in groupEvalRobustness.test.ts/fairness-guard.test.ts under test:unit.
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract
evidence: Probe 2026-09-23 (PYTHONPATH=. python, keyless): job = mkjob(seniority='senior', must-have Python); pool = [('id-a', senior bau 'X'), ('id-b', junior bau 'Y')]. ('Jan Novák','Jan Novák') -> koFailed ['id-b'] ranking [] ids ['id-a','id-b']; ('Jan Novák','Petr Svoboda') -> koFailed ['id-b'] ranking ['Jan Novák']. recruiter.py:66 `ko_failed_labels.add(cand.label)`; :68 `matrix["ranking"] = [label for label in matrix["ranking"] if label not in ko_failed_labels]`. groupEvalTypes.ts:76 `if (ranking.length + koCount !== n) return false;` -> 0 + 1 != 2 -> not aligned -> assessRobustness 'unavailable'. groupEvalHelpers.ts:94 `const projected = headlineOrder.filter((l) => inMatrix.has(l));` compares names only.
